label: Phase 001: the seven activity group titles are liftable verbatim from ACTIVITY_GROUPS (activity-groups.ts:28-39) and the plan fixes only the ids, so a builder invents seven labels the screen sample must then match.

Phase 001: stopped is a derived predicate over a nullable stoppedAt instant (queries.ts:300-304, activity-groups.ts:82-87), not a status value, so the fix needs no new status, no index column and no SCHEMA_VERSION move.
Phase 001: the reference dedupes a needs-you item against the run that raised it (activity-groups.ts:147-152) and the plan does not, so one parked run prints under both needs_you and working.

Phase 001: oneRowPerAction drops an action first row when its failure row is loaded beside it (activity-rows.ts:70-96) and the plan has no rule for the queue three-attempt retry, so one request can print two rows.

Phase 002: FIRING_FRAME (routine-firing.ts:9-13) exists because a live firing read its own instruction as a routine-management question, did nothing and recorded succeeded; phase 002 changes when a bot runs and never what the run is told.

Phase 002: checkInSubject (plan.ts:52-68) records a live identity collision where every unnamed tell routine landed on the default check-in and was refused as already there; the plan does: tell has no identity rule.

Phase 002: the plan sorts recurring by next fire and the reference never time-sorts it (activity-groups.ts:175-192); the evidence supports the plan for a terminal list but the reference stable order avoids rows moving under the reader.
